scenes.title: Gray Life on the Prairie
scenes.summary: The gray Kansas prairie, the small one-room house with its cyclone cellar, and the joyless lives of Uncle Henry and Aunt Em contrasted with Dorothy's laughter kept alive by playful Toto.

scenes.title: The Cyclone Approaches
scenes.summary: Anxious watching turns to alarm as winds gather from north and south; Uncle Henry runs to the stock while Aunt Em screams for Dorothy to reach the cellar, but chasing Toto delays their escape as the wind shrieks and shakes the house.

scenes.title: Lifted Into the Sky
scenes.summary: The house whirls, lifts, and balances at the still center of the cyclone, carried miles away like a feather while Dorothy feels as if rising in a balloon.

scenes.title: Riding Calm to Sleep
scenes.summary: Rocked gently in the dark howling wind, Dorothy sits still, rescues Toto from the open trap door, then grows lonely but calm through the long hours until both curl up on the bed and fall asleep.

muse_override.reason: Gentle cradle rocking to sleep dominates despite lingering howling wind and loneliness.

scenes.title: Awakening in a Beautiful Country
scenes.summary: Dorothy wakes after the cyclone shock to bright sunshine and stillness, opens the door to a marvelous beautiful country, and sees a group of strange little people approaching her house.

scenes.title: You Killed the Wicked Witch
scenes.summary: The old woman welcomes Dorothy as a noble Sorceress for killing the Wicked Witch of the East. Horrified, Dorothy learns her house fell on the witch, whose silver-shod feet stick out from under the beam.

scenes.title: Good Witches and the Great Wizard
scenes.summary: Dorothy learns who the Munchkins are, that her greeter is the good Witch of the North, that only two good and two wicked witches remain in uncivilized Oz, and that the Great Wizard Oz lives in the City of Emeralds.

muse_override.reason: Calm exposition builds wonder and mystery about good witches and the Great Wizard.

scenes.title: The Silver Shoes Remain
scenes.summary: The Munchkins shout as the dead witch's feet vanish in the sun, leaving only the silver shoes, which the Witch of the North gives to Dorothy as a charmed gift.

muse_override.reason: Vanished feet and enchanted silver shoes create mystery and wonder amid joyful relief.

scenes.title: No Way Home
scenes.summary: Dorothy begs for help returning to Kansas, but the Munchkins and the Witch explain desert surrounds Oz on all sides and the West is ruled by a Wicked Witch, leaving her to sob at having to stay.

scenes.title: Kiss of Protection and the Yellow Brick Road
scenes.summary: By slate magic the Witch directs Dorothy to the City of Emeralds, kisses her forehead for protection, tells her to follow the yellow brick road to Oz, then vanishes as the Munchkins wish her a pleasant journey.

muse_override.reason: Tearful goodbye shifts to hopeful protection and magical departure toward adventure.

scenes.title: Morning Preparations
scenes.summary: Alone in the house, Dorothy eats breakfast with Toto, washes and dresses in clean gingham, finds the Witch's silver shoes fit perfectly, packs bread, locks up, and sets out for the Emerald City.

scenes.title: The Yellow Brick Road
scenes.summary: Dorothy walks briskly along the yellow brick road in bright sunshine past blue fences and farms, greeted with bows, until evening when she reaches a large house with dancing and feasting.

muse_override.reason: Bright sunny walk with merry music, dancing, and hopeful journey to Emerald City.

scenes.title: Feast at Boq's House
scenes.summary: The rich Munchkin Boq welcomes Dorothy to supper and lodging to celebrate freedom from the Witch; she eats, watches dancing, is mistaken for a friendly witch, and sleeps soundly.

scenes.title: Warning and Farewell
scenes.summary: Over breakfast Dorothy learns the Emerald City is many days away through rough and dangerous places, but bravely resolves to continue because only Oz can send her to Kansas.

scenes.title: The Winking Scarecrow Rescued
scenes.summary: Resting by a cornfield, Dorothy sees a straw Scarecrow wink and nod, speaks with him, and lifts him off his pole, freeing him as he thanks her like a new man.

scenes.title: A New Companion Joins
scenes.summary: Dorothy invites the brainless Scarecrow to join her to ask Oz for brains; they return to the road together with Toto wary, as the Scarecrow confides his only fear is a lighted match.

scenes.title: Rough Road and Midday Rest
scenes.summary: The yellow brick road grows rough, broken, and lonely as farms disappear. Dorothy, Toto, and the stumbling, laughing Scarecrow stop by a brook at noon for bread, which the Scarecrow refuses because his mouth is only painted.

scenes.title: No Place Like Home
scenes.summary: Resting by the roadside, Dorothy tells of gray Kansas and the cyclone that brought her to Oz. The Scarecrow cannot understand wanting to leave beauty for home, and Dorothy answers there is no place like home.

scenes.title: The Scarecrow's Making
scenes.summary: Asked for a story, the Scarecrow recounts being made only the day before yesterday, painted ear by ear and eye by eye, set on a pole, exposed by an old crow, and resolved to seek brains from Oz. Dorothy promises hope and they set off again.

scenes.title: Into the Dark Forest
scenes.summary: Toward evening the travelers reach a great forest where big close trees shut out daylight over the yellow bricks. They press on into the gloom, joking that the road that goes in must come out at the Emerald City.

muse_override.reason: Dark enclosing forest on the onward road blends mystery and adventure with light suspense.

scenes.title: Night Shelter in the Cottage
scenes.summary: Night falls and they stumble in darkness, Dorothy guided on the Scarecrow's arm with Toto seeing ahead. The Scarecrow spots a log cottage where Dorothy and Toto sleep on leaves while the tireless Scarecrow waits for morning.

scenes.title: Morning Awakening and Breakfast
scenes.summary: Dorothy wakes to bright morning forest. She and the patient Scarecrow leave the cottage to find a spring where she washes, drinks, and eats, worrying that little bread remains for her and Toto.

muse_override.reason: Peaceful sunny morning with washing and breakfast at the spring conveys calm and gentle joy.

scenes.title: Mysterious Groans in the Forest
scenes.summary: A deep groan startles Dorothy. Following the sound through the trees, they discover a motionless man made entirely of tin, axe raised, shining in the sun, while Toto snaps at his legs.

scenes.title: The Oiling and Rescue
scenes.summary: The rusted tin man explains he has groaned unheard for a year and needs oil. Dorothy fetches his oil-can and together they oil his neck, arms, and legs until he moves freely, lowers his axe, and thanks them for saving his life.

muse_override.reason: Gentle rescue and grateful relief create warm joyful comfort after sadness.

scenes.title: A New Companion Joins
scenes.summary: Learning they seek Oz, the Tin Woodman asks for a heart and joins the party. They return to the yellow brick road, bringing his oil-can, and he proves his worth by chopping through thick branches blocking their way.

scenes.title: Brains Versus Heart Debate
scenes.summary: Walking on, the Scarecrow falls in a hole and cheerful talk turns to a friendly debate over brains versus heart, prompting the Tin Woodman to promise his own story to explain why he prefers a heart.

scenes.title: The Tin Woodman's Tragic Tale
scenes.summary: The Tin Woodman recounts his tragic transformation: a Munchkin woodman in love, cursed by the Wicked Witch of the East through an enchanted axe, gradually replaced limb by limb with tin until he lost his heart and then rusted helpless in the rain.

scenes.title: Reflections and Dwindling Bread
scenes.summary: Moved by the story, Scarecrow still wants brains while Tin Woodman wants a heart for happiness. Dorothy stays puzzled and privately worried as the bread is nearly gone and only she and Toto need to eat.

muse_override.reason: Calm philosophical reflection dominates with gentle worry over dwindling bread.

scenes.title: Fear in the Thick Forest
scenes.summary: The group treks through a dark, overgrown forest road as distant growls frighten Dorothy, while the Tin Woodman reassures her of their protections.

scenes.title: Lion Ambush
scenes.summary: A great Lion bursts onto the road, scattering the Scarecrow and felling the Tin Woodman, then turns on Toto until Dorothy bravely rushes in to slap him.

scenes.title: A Scolded Beast
scenes.summary: Scolded by Dorothy, the sheepish Lion apologizes and marvels that the Scarecrow is stuffed, the Woodman is tin, and Toto is a tiny meat dog.

muse_override.reason: Shamed lion's apology under Dorothy's scolding softens into gentle comic curiosity.

scenes.title: Confession of the Coward
scenes.summary: The Lion confesses his lifelong cowardice despite being King of Beasts, weeping that his heart pounds with fear whenever there is danger.

scenes.title: Joining the Quest for Courage
scenes.summary: Learning they seek brains, a heart, and a return to Kansas from Oz, the Lion begs to join them to ask for courage and is welcomed as a protector.

scenes.title: Peaceful Road and Rusted Tears
scenes.summary: The enlarged party journeys on in peace as Toto befriends the Lion, until the weeping Woodman rusts his jaws over a crushed beetle and is oiled back to speech.

muse_override.reason: Peaceful companionship dominates with gentle sadness over the beetle and brief worry at rusted jaws.

scenes.title: Night Camp in the Forest
scenes.summary: The travelers camp under a tree with fire and food, sleeping safely, then wake and set out for the Emerald City in daylight.

scenes.title: Blocked by the First Ditch
scenes.summary: The party is blocked by a wide, deep ditch with jagged rocks and despairs until the Lion offers to carry them over one by one.

scenes.title: Leaping Across
scenes.summary: The Lion leaps the gulf with the Scarecrow, Dorothy and Toto, and the Tin Woodman, landing safely and resting afterward.

scenes.title: Dark Woods and the Fallen Tree Bridge
scenes.summary: Entering dark, gloomy woods haunted by Kalidahs, they find a second impassable gulf and fell a tree to make a bridge.

scenes.title: Kalidah Attack
scenes.summary: Two monstrous Kalidahs attack on the tree bridge; the Lion roars and retreats while the Woodman chops the tree, sending the beasts to their doom.

scenes.title: River Vista and Rest
scenes.summary: Relieved, the travelers hurry to a broad river overlooking sunny meadows, eat fruit, start a raft, and sleep dreaming of Oz.

muse_override.reason: Joyful river vista, fruit meal, and cozy sleep bring calm relief and happiness after anxious travel.

scenes.title: Morning Hope at the River
scenes.summary: Refreshed after the forest, the party breakfasts by the river and finishes the log raft to cross toward the sunny country and the Emerald City.

scenes.title: Swept Away and Stranded
scenes.summary: The swift current drags the raft from the Yellow Brick Road; the Scarecrow's pole sticks in the mud and he is left clinging alone mid-river while his friends float on, fearing the Wicked Witch of the West.

muse_override.reason: Swift current danger and Scarecrow abandoned on pole blend suspense with sorrow.

scenes.title: Lion's Swim to Shore
scenes.summary: The Lion swims ashore pulling the raft by his tail, and the exhausted party lands far downstream and plans to walk back along the bank to regain the road.

muse_override.reason: Strenuous rescue swim resolves into sunny calm shore with lingering sadness for the Scarecrow.

scenes.title: The Stork Rescue
scenes.summary: Spotting the lonely Scarecrow on his pole, Dorothy enlists a passing Stork to lift his light straw body back to the bank, leading to a joyful reunion and farewell to the kind bird.

scenes.title: Beauty of the Poppy Meadow
scenes.summary: Walking through thickening brilliant flowers, the companions admire the beautiful scarlet poppy meadow, unaware its powerful scent brings deadly sleep.

muse_override.reason: Beautiful dazzling meadow invites calm wonder, with growing drowsy threat underneath.

scenes.title: Deadly Sleep and Desperate Carry
scenes.summary: Dorothy, Toto, and then the Lion succumb to the poppy poison; the untiring Scarecrow and Tin Woodman carry Dorothy out in a hand-chair, forced to leave the heavy Lion sleeping at the field's edge until they reach fresh grass by the river.

scenes.title: Wildcat Attack
scenes.summary: Near the road the party is ambushed by a great yellow Wildcat chasing a little gray field mouse. The Tin Woodman intervenes and beheads the beast with his axe.

muse_override.reason: Sudden wildcat charge and axe beheading create urgent combat with suspense.

scenes.title: The Mouse Queen's Gratitude
scenes.summary: The rescued mouse thanks the Woodman and reveals herself as Queen of all the Field Mice. Her subjects rush in, bow to her, and pledge to serve the Tin Woodman for saving her.

scenes.title: Toto Scatters the Mice
scenes.summary: Toto wakes and gleefully charges into the mice, scattering them. The Woodman restrains him and reassures the frightened Queen until the mice timidly creep back.

scenes.title: A Plan to Save the Lion
scenes.summary: Asked how to repay him, the mice learn of the Cowardly Lion asleep in the poppies. The Scarecrow promises the Lion will not harm them and has the Queen summon thousands of mice, each with a string.

scenes.title: The Mouse-Drawn Rescue
scenes.summary: The Woodman builds a wooden truck while thousands of string-bearing mice assemble. Harnessed to the truck, they haul the heavy Lion, pushed by his friends, out of the poisonous poppy bed to fresh air.

scenes.title: Farewell and Vigil
scenes.summary: Dorothy thanks the mice as they are unharnessed. The Queen promises future help, bids goodbye, and runs off while Toto is held back. The friends sit beside the sleeping Lion while Dorothy eats.

scenes.title: Lion Wakes and the Road Regained
scenes.summary: The Cowardly Lion wakes from the poppies alive thanks to the field mice. Relieved and refreshed, the companions laugh together and set off again through fresh grass until they regain the yellow brick road toward the Emerald City.

scenes.title: Entering the Green Country
scenes.summary: The road becomes smooth and the country turns beautifully green, with green houses, green clothes, and fearful onlookers. Dorothy realizes this is the Land of Oz, but the Scarecrow worries the people seem unfriendly and they need food and shelter.

scenes.title: Shelter at the Farmhouse
scenes.summary: Dorothy boldly knocks at a farmhouse. The woman is frightened of the Lion, but Dorothy reassures her he is tame and cowardly. After hesitation, the woman invites the strange company inside for supper and sleep.

scenes.title: Tales of the Terrible Oz
scenes.summary: Inside, the injured farmer warns them that Oz never lets anyone see him and sits unseen in his Throne Room. He describes Oz as a Great Wizard who can take any form - bird, elephant, cat, fairy. Each traveler states their wish for brains, heart, courage, and home, which the farmer says Oz could grant, if they can ever get to see him.

scenes.title: Supper and Guarded Rest
scenes.summary: The mood softens into domestic comfort as they eat supper - Dorothy enjoying porridge and eggs while Toto eats well and the Lion disdains oats. Dorothy sleeps in a bed guarded by the Lion while the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman keep quiet watch, then they leave at sunrise.

scenes.title: The Green Glow and the Great Wall
scenes.summary: On the road they see a green glow that brightens as they approach the end of their travels. By afternoon they reach the high thick green wall, the emerald-studded gate, and Dorothy rings the bell to be admitted to a glittering arched hall.

scenes.title: Guardian of the Gate and Green Spectacles
scenes.summary: A little green man, the Guardian of the Gates, warns that Oz is powerful and terrible to the dishonest and curious, but agrees to take them to the Palace. He explains the blinding glory of the City and locks green spectacles on Dorothy, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, the Lion, and Toto, then unlocks the inner gate to lead them into the Emerald City.

scenes.title: Arrival in the Emerald City
scenes.summary: Protected by green spectacles, Dorothy and her friends enter and marvel at the all-green, emerald-studded City, its green-clad people, green goods, and happy prosperity.

scenes.title: The Palace Gates and Oz's Rule
scenes.summary: Led to the Palace of Oz, the party is received by a green-uniformed soldier who carries their message behind the screen and returns with Oz's rule: each must enter alone, one per day, requiring a multi-day stay.

muse_override.reason: The unseen Oz behind his screen and grand green palace create mystery and awe.

scenes.title: Rooms for the Night
scenes.summary: A green girl leads Dorothy to a lovely green bedroom and settles the others in pleasant rooms, where each passes the night in his own way, from staring to oiling joints to purring asleep.

muse_override.reason: Cozy green rooms and quiet night rest evoke calm with gentle wonder.

scenes.title: Summoned to the Throne
scenes.summary: In the morning Dorothy is dressed in green finery and led toward the Throne Room past curious courtiers, while the soldier explains Oz's anger turned to interest by her silver shoes and forehead mark.
characters: Ladies and gentlemen of the court

muse_override.reason: Whispered warnings, the bell, and entering alone build suspense, mystery, and awe.

scenes.title: Dorothy Meets the Great Head
scenes.summary: Alone in the emerald Throne Room, Dorothy confronts the enormous bodiless Head of Oz, answers his sharp questions about her silver shoes and the Good Witch's kiss, and asks to be sent to Kansas.

scenes.title: The Price: Kill the Wicked Witch
scenes.summary: Oz refuses free help and names his price: Dorothy must kill the Wicked Witch of the West. She weeps and protests she never killed willingly, but Oz dismisses her until the task is done.

scenes.title: Sorrowful News
scenes.summary: Dorothy sorrowfully reports no hope to her waiting friends and cries herself to sleep; next morning the soldier fetches the Scarecrow for his solitary audience.

scenes.title: The Scarecrow and the Lovely Lady
scenes.summary: Astonished to find Oz as a winged, beautiful Lady instead of a Head, the Scarecrow begs for brains and is likewise told to earn them by killing the Wicked Witch of the West.

muse_override.reason: Awe at Oz appearing as lovely winged Lady dominates with mysterious undertone.

scenes.title: The Woodman and the Beast
scenes.summary: The Tin Woodman finds Oz transformed into a five-eyed, five-limbed Beast, pleads for a heart, receives the same condition to help kill the Witch, and the friends marvel while the Lion boasts he will frighten Oz.

muse_override.reason: Terrible five-eyed Beast inspires mystery, awe and suspense with disappointed sadness.

scenes.title: The Lion and the Ball of Fire
scenes.summary: The Lion faces Oz as a fierce, scorching Ball of Fire, begs for courage, is told courage requires proof of the Witch's death, and flees the heat to report to his friends.
characters: Oz as the Ball of Fire

muse_override.reason: Trembling Lion facing the burning, speaking Ball of Fire evokes mystery, suspense and awe.

scenes.title: Resolve to Seek the Witch
scenes.summary: With all hopes barred until the Witch dies, the friends resolve to journey to the Winkies despite fear and reluctance, prepare axe, straw, paint and provisions, and sleep before an early start.

scenes.title: Leaving the Emerald City
scenes.summary: Freed from the Emerald City, Dorothy and her friends learn no road leads west and set out on foot across soft fields that grow rough and hilly, ending their first day tired and asleep under guard.

scenes.title: Attack of the Wolves
scenes.summary: Spying the travelers with her telescopic eye, the Wicked Witch sends forty wolves to tear them apart, but the Tin Woodman stands guard and chops them all down while the others sleep.

scenes.title: Attack of the Crows
scenes.summary: Enraged by the dead wolves, the Witch sends a dark flock of crows. The Scarecrow takes his turn to fight, terrifying the birds and twisting the necks of all forty, including their king.

scenes.title: Attack of the Bees
scenes.summary: The Witch unleashes stinging black bees, but the Scarecrow hides Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion under his straw while the bees break their stings on tin and die.

muse_override.reason: Furious bee swarm attack is tense combat cleverly foiled by straw cover and tin immunity.

scenes.title: The Last Charm
scenes.summary: Her beasts defeated, the Witch sends her Winkie slaves with spears, who flee from the Lion's roar. Furious, she resolves to spend her last use of the charmed Golden Cap that commands the Winged Monkeys.

scenes.title: Summoning the Winged Monkeys
scenes.summary: The Witch dons the Golden Cap and chants the three-part spell. The sky darkens with rushing wings as the Winged Monkeys arrive for their third and final obedience.

scenes.title: The Companions Destroyed
scenes.summary: The Monkeys batter the Woodman on sharp rocks, empty the Scarecrow into a tree, and cage the bound Lion, but spare Dorothy because of the Good Witch's kiss, carrying her gently to the castle.

muse_override.reason: Friends are violently destroyed while Dorothy is helplessly spared, blending sorrow with tense dread.

scenes.title: Dorothy Enslaved
scenes.summary: Cowed by Dorothy's forehead mark and Silver Shoes, the Witch instead enslaves her, forcing her to clean and cook in the castle kitchen while plotting to steal her power.

scenes.title: Nights with the Lion
scenes.summary: The Lion refuses to be harnessed and is starved, but Dorothy secretly feeds him at night and they mourn together. The Witch dares not truly strike Dorothy, though she hits Toto.

scenes.title: The Stolen Shoe
scenes.summary: Coveting the Silver Shoes but fearing dark and water, the Witch trips Dorothy with invisible iron to snatch one shoe, then gloats and refuses to return it as Dorothy's anger boils over.

muse_override.reason: Cunning theft and angry confrontation build tense suspense with looming magical showdown.

scenes.title: The Melting
scenes.summary: In fury Dorothy dashes water on the Witch, who shrieks, shrinks, and melts into a brown mass. Dorothy washes her away, reclaims the shoe, and runs to free the Lion.

scenes.title: Freedom for the Winkies
scenes.summary: Dorothy frees the Lion and declares the Winkies no longer slaves, sparking joyful feasting and dancing across the Yellow Castle.

scenes.title: The Search for the Tin Woodman
scenes.summary: Missing their friends, Dorothy and the Lion enlist the Winkies to search for the Tin Woodman, finding him battered on the rocky plain and carrying him tearfully back to the castle.

muse_override.reason: Hopeful rescue expedition turns sorrowful upon finding the battered Tin Woodman.

scenes.title: Mended with Patches
scenes.summary: Winkie tinsmiths hammer and solder the Tin Woodman back into shape over three days, leading to a tearful, joyful reunion with Dorothy and the Lion.

scenes.title: Recovering the Scarecrow
scenes.summary: The reunited friends set out again to rescue the Scarecrow, chopping down the tall tree with a new gold-handled axe to recover his clothes and stuff him with fresh straw.

scenes.title: Farewell and New Journey
scenes.summary: After happy days together, the friends resolve to return to Oz, bid farewell with gifts from the grateful Winkies, and set out for the Emerald City with Dorothy wearing the Golden Cap.

scenes.title: Lost in the Scarlet Fields
scenes.summary: After leaving the Witch's castle on foot, the travelers lose their way in endless fields of buttercups and daisies, growing tired and disheartened as days pass with no sign of the Emerald City.

muse_override.reason: Weary wandering through endless fields where hope fades into sadness yet travel continues.

scenes.title: The Queen's Advice
scenes.summary: Dorothy blows her whistle to summon the field mice, and the Queen tells her the Emerald City lies behind them and reveals the charm written inside the Golden Cap to command the Winged Monkeys.

scenes.title: Summoning the Winged Monkeys
scenes.summary: Dorothy reads and speaks the Cap's charm, summoning the Winged Monkeys who seize the party and bear them cheerfully through the air toward the Emerald City.

muse_override.reason: Magical chant summons monkeys for wonder-filled aerial adventure.

scenes.title: Tale of the Golden Cap
scenes.summary: During the flight the Monkey King tells how his people pranked Quelala, were punished by sorceress Gayelette, and were bound to obey thrice whoever owns the Golden Cap.

muse_override.reason: A leisurely in-flight folktale of ancient magic and lost freedom blends calm storytelling with wonder and wistful regret.

scenes.title: Arrival at the Emerald City
scenes.summary: The Monkeys set the travelers safely down before the green walls of the Emerald City and fly away as Dorothy and the Lion rejoice at their swift rescue.

muse_override.reason: Joyful relief and wonder as travelers gaze at the shining green walls after rescue.

scenes.title: Return to the Emerald City
scenes.summary: The travelers return in triumph after melting the Wicked Witch, are welcomed by the city, then grow vexed as Oz avoids them for days until a threat of the Winged Monkeys forces him to summon them.

muse_override.reason: Triumphant return brings joy and wonder, then tense waiting and Oz's evasion builds suspense and mystery.

scenes.title: The Voice in the Empty Throne
scenes.summary: After a sleepless night of hope, the friends enter an empty, dreadfully still Throne Room where the invisible voice of Oz evades their demands until the Lion's roar tips the corner screen.

scenes.title: The Humbug Exposed
scenes.summary: The fallen screen reveals a frightened little old man; shock turns to dismay as Dorothy and her friends realize the Great and Terrible Oz is only a humbug making believe.

scenes.title: Tricks of the False Wizard
scenes.summary: Oz begs them to keep his secret and leads them to his workshop to demonstrate the paper Head, Lady costume, Beast skins, and cotton Ball of Fire and ventriloquism.

muse_override.reason: Oz reveals his stage tricks, blending behind-the-curtain mystery with wonder and sheepish humor.

scenes.title: The Balloonist from Omaha
scenes.summary: Oz tells his story of being a ventriloquist and circus balloonist from Omaha, blown to Oz, building the Emerald City with green spectacles, and living in fear of the Witches.

scenes.title: Promises for Tomorrow
scenes.summary: Chastened but kindly, Oz promises brains, courage, and a heart tomorrow and time to find Dorothy a way to Kansas, and the friends return to their rooms in high spirits.

muse_override.reason: Promises of brains, heart, courage and home fill the palace with hopeful joyful relief.

scenes.title: The Scarecrow Gets His Bran-New Brains
scenes.summary: The Scarecrow cheerfully leaves his friends to claim his wish. In the Throne Room, Oz removes his straw-stuffed head and fills it with bran mixed with pins and needles. Proud of his bulging new brains, he returns to Dorothy and his friends, who tease that the pins prove he is sharp.

scenes.title: The Tin Woodman Gets His Silk Heart
scenes.summary: The Tin Woodman enters the Throne Room for his heart. Oz cuts a square hole in his tin breast and inserts a pretty silk heart stuffed with sawdust, soldering the patch neatly. Delighted and grateful, the Woodman rejoins his friends to celebrate his good fortune.

scenes.title: The Lion Drinks His Courage
scenes.summary: The Cowardly Lion enters for his courage. Oz pours a mysterious liquid from a green bottle into a carved dish and tells him courage must be inside to work. The Lion drinks it all, declares himself full of courage, and joyfully returns to tell his friends.

scenes.title: The Humbug Reflects Alone
scenes.summary: Left alone, Oz smiles at his humbug success in making the three friends happy with what they merely imagined they wanted, then turns anxious and rueful as he admits he does not know how he can ever carry Dorothy back to Kansas.

muse_override.reason: Oz's quiet self-doubt mixes calm reflection with sad uncertainty about Dorothy.

scenes.title: Sad Waiting and a Summons
scenes.summary: After three sad days of waiting while her companions feel content with their new gifts, Dorothy still longs for Kansas until Oz finally sends for her and promises he has found a way out across the desert.

muse_override.reason: Sad waiting yields to hopeful summons, mixing sorrow and suspense with emerging adventure.

scenes.title: The Balloon Plan
scenes.summary: In the Throne Room Oz explains his plan to build a hot-air silk balloon to fly over the desert, confesses he is tired of being a humbug and wants to return with her, and the two spend three days sewing and gluing the green silk bag and fitting a basket.

scenes.title: Inflation and Farewell
scenes.summary: Before a curious crowd Oz has the balloon carried out and inflated over a wood fire until it tugs at its ropes, then climbs in and proclaims the Scarecrow will rule in his absence while urging Dorothy to hurry aboard.

muse_override.reason: Balloon inflation inspires wonder with tense anticipation and adventurous farewell.

scenes.title: Left Behind
scenes.summary: Delayed finding Toto, Dorothy reaches for Oz's hands just as the ropes break and the balloon rises without her; despite cries of goodbye the Wizard vanishes forever, and the people lovingly remember him while grieving his loss for many days.

scenes.title: Mourning Oz
scenes.summary: Dorothy and her friends mourn Oz's departure, and the Tin Woodman weeps over losing the giver of his heart until Dorothy wipes his tears and he oils himself.

scenes.title: Council in the Throne Room
scenes.summary: The Scarecrow rules the Emerald City and holds council with the others; all are content except Dorothy, who wants Kansas, prompting the Scarecrow to suggest the Winged Monkeys.

muse_override.reason: Warm contented reunion with joyful hopeful plan to return home.

scenes.title: The Refusal of the Monkeys
scenes.summary: Dorothy summons the Winged Monkeys to carry her to Kansas, but the Monkey King explains they cannot leave Oz country and departs, leaving her disappointed.

scenes.title: News of Glinda
scenes.summary: After the failure, the Scarecrow calls the soldier with green whiskers, who tells them only Glinda, the Good Witch of the South, might help, though the southern road is full of dangers.

scenes.title: Vow to Journey South
scenes.summary: The friends resolve that Dorothy must travel south to Glinda, and the Lion, Woodman, and Scarecrow all vow to accompany and protect her, planning to start in the morning.

scenes.title: Farewell to the Emerald City
scenes.summary: The party says goodbye at the gates of the Emerald City, returns their spectacles, and sets out south in bright, hopeful spirits, chatting fondly about Oz and camping peacefully under the stars.

scenes.title: Attacked by the Fighting Trees
scenes.summary: The travelers reach an impassable thick wood and try to enter, but the living branches seize and hurl the Scarecrow back twice until the Tin Woodman chops his way through and frees the party, including Toto.

scenes.title: The China Wall Beyond the Wood
scenes.summary: Having passed the outer guard-trees unharmed, the friends walk easily to the far edge of the forest only to be stopped by a high, smooth white china wall, which the Tin Woodman proposes to climb with a ladder.

muse_override.reason: Unexpected china wall blocks easy walk, sparking wonder and adventurous ladder plan.

scenes.title: Climbing the Wall
scenes.summary: The travelers wake and climb the Woodman's ladder to the top of the wall, each crying out in wonder as they see what lies beyond.

scenes.title: First Sight of China Country
scenes.summary: Looking down, the party beholds the shining white Dainty China Country with its tiny painted houses, animals, and fragile china people.

scenes.title: The Broken Cow
scenes.summary: The travelers descend into the fragile country and carefully start across, but frighten a milkmaid's cow, breaking its leg and learning they must tread very gently.

scenes.title: Princess and Clown
scenes.summary: Dorothy meets a beautiful china Princess and a cracked clown who rhymes and stands on his head, and learns why the china folk prefer to stay in their own country.

muse_override.reason: Fragile china beauty and silly cracked clown create light wonder and playful joy.

scenes.title: Leaving China Country
scenes.summary: The party hurries across the country to the far wall, escaping with only a broken church, and reflects on their luck and fragility.

scenes.title: Through Bogs to the Ancient Forest
scenes.summary: The travelers pick their way through bogs and underbrush into a vast old forest. The Lion is delighted by the soft leaves and moss while the Scarecrow finds it gloomy, and the party camps for the night with Dorothy, Toto, and the Lion sleeping while the Woodman and Scarecrow keep watch.

muse_override.reason: Trek through bogs into a vast old forest blends adventure and mystery with looming suspense and quiet wonder.

scenes.title: The Council of Beasts
scenes.summary: In the morning the party hears growling and finds hundreds of beasts holding a troubled meeting. The tiger welcomes the Lion as King of Beasts and explains they are terrorized by a giant man-eating spider-monster. The Lion bargains that if he kills it, they will bow to him and obey him as King of the Forest, and they roar agreement.

scenes.title: Lion Against the Spider
scenes.summary: The tiger points out the monster among the oaks. The Lion leaves his friends in the beasts' care, marches off, finds the spider asleep, and kills it with a spring onto its back and one clawed blow that severs its slender neck from its body.

scenes.title: Crowned King of the Forest
scenes.summary: The Lion returns proudly to announce the enemy is dead. The beasts bow down to him as their King, and he promises to come back and rule over them once Dorothy is safely on her way to Kansas.

scenes.title: The Hill Bars the Way
scenes.summary: The travelers leave the forest and face a steep rocky hill, where a strange armless man claims the hill and forbids them to cross on their way to the Quadlings.

muse_override.reason: A blocked climb and threatening voice create tense suspense with adventurous defiance.

scenes.title: Attack of the Hammer-Heads
scenes.summary: The Hammer-Heads reveal their shooting-head attack, knocking down the Scarecrow and the Lion while hundreds laugh from the rocks, proving force is useless.

scenes.title: Rescue by the Winged Monkeys
scenes.summary: On the Tin Woodman's advice Dorothy uses the Golden Cap for the last time but one, and the Winged Monkeys carry the party safely over the hill and bid farewell.

scenes.title: Arrival in the Quadling Country
scenes.summary: Safe in the rich red Quadling country, the travelers eat at a farmhouse, learn Glinda's castle is near, and are admitted at its gates to see the Good Witch.

muse_override.reason: Rich happy fields, kind meal, and beautiful castle create calm joy with light onward adventure.

scenes.title: Audience with Glinda
scenes.summary: After freshening up, the friends are led into Glinda's throne room, where the beautiful young Good Witch in white on a ruby throne kindly asks how she can help.

scenes.title: Dorothy's Wish and the Bargain
scenes.summary: Dorothy recounts her adventures and her wish to return to Kansas, and Glinda promises a way home in exchange for the now-useless Golden Cap.

muse_override.reason: Tender goodbye bargain brings warm hopeful joy with gentle wonder and calm.

scenes.title: Kingdoms Promised to Three Friends
scenes.summary: Glinda asks each companion's future and pledges the Cap's three commands to carry the Scarecrow to Emerald City, the Woodman to the Winkies, and the Lion to his forest before freeing the Monkeys.

scenes.title: The Secret of the Silver Shoes
scenes.summary: Glinda reveals the Silver Shoes can carry Dorothy anywhere in three steps, prompting joyful reflection on their journey and Dorothy's resolve to go home at once.

muse_override.reason: Bittersweet happy farewell with wonder at the magical shoes carrying her home.

scenes.title: Tearful Farewell and Flight
scenes.summary: Through tears Dorothy embraces and kisses her friends and Glinda goodbye, then with Toto in her arms clicks her heels three times and whirls into the air.

scenes.title: Home on the Kansas Prairie
scenes.summary: In three steps Dorothy tumbles onto the Kansas prairie before the new farmhouse, finding Toto running to the barn while her Silver Shoes are lost forever in the desert.

muse_override.reason: Sudden magical return brings joyful wonder settling into warm prairie calm with faint loss for the shoes.

scenes.title: Home Again
scenes.summary: Aunt Em finds Dorothy running toward her outside the house and embraces her with kisses, asking where she came from. Dorothy answers gravely that she is back from the Land of Oz with Toto, overjoyed to be home again.
